cases.title: Login and role routing
cases.source: FS pp. 6, 10-11, Authentication; TS pp. 11, 24; D01
cases.steps: Log in as Student/Staff, Technician and Admin; repeat with invalid credentials.
cases.expected: Valid users reach the correct role dashboard using a secure session; invalid login shows a clear error. Student entry follows approved D01.

cases.title: Profile and role administration
cases.source: FS pp. 6-7, 9; TS p. 9, User Overview
cases.steps: Review a user profile and exercise authorized user and role management; repeat as an ordinary user.
cases.expected: Names, NWU email and assigned roles persist correctly; only authorized administrators can change permissions.

cases.title: Structured fault submission
cases.source: FS p. 11, Ticket Logging; TS pp. 13-14, FR1.1
cases.steps: Submit title, detailed description, category, location, lab station ID and urgency from the portal.
cases.expected: The form captures all required fault details, uses predefined categories and urgency selections, and confirms a successful submission.

cases.title: Required fields and email validation
cases.source: FS pp. 11, 13, Error Prevention; TS p. 18, 3.5.3
cases.steps: Omit each mandatory field, enter invalid field values and an invalid NWU email, then correct them.
cases.expected: Clear validation prevents incomplete or invalid tickets; corrected input is accepted. Record the approved institutional email domains.

cases.title: Unique identity and ticket persistence
cases.steps: Create multiple tickets, reload them and inspect their saved records with an authorized tester.
cases.expected: Each ticket has a unique Ticket ID, creation time, correct reporter association and initial state; all fields persist in MongoDB. See D04.

cases.title: Urgency and queue ordering
cases.steps: Create Low, Medium and High urgency tickets and inspect the technician queue.
cases.expected: Priority is saved accurately and organizes the queue so higher urgency work is visible first; hazardous priority is tested separately in T cases.

cases.title: Reporter ticket visibility
cases.steps: As two different reporters, view recent requests, open a ticket and track its status; try the other reporter ticket.
cases.expected: Each reporter sees their own requests and status history; another reporter ticket is inaccessible through both UI and API.

cases.title: Technician queue and filters
cases.steps: Open the technician dashboard, filter each lifecycle state and inspect priority ordering and ticket cards.
cases.expected: Authorized technicians see the permitted queue, status filters and history; cards show station ID, priority and time since submission. Labels follow D04.

cases.title: Claim and technician assignment
cases.source: TS p. 14, Feature 2 sequence; FS p. 6; D04
cases.steps: Claim a pending ticket and reopen it as the assigned technician.
cases.expected: The ticket records the technician and claim time, moves to the approved active state and updates the dashboard and history.

cases.title: Controlled lifecycle changes
cases.steps: Move a ticket through each approved state and attempt an unsupported state change.
cases.expected: Only approved transitions succeed; the ticket, queue and audit history remain consistent for New/Pending, Assigned, In Progress, Escalated and Resolved as agreed.

cases.title: Start and stop job card timer
cases.source: FS pp. 11-12, Job Cards; PP Appendix A UAT-02
cases.steps: Start a timer, wait a measured interval and stop it; inspect the job card and time log.
cases.expected: Start and stop timestamps persist, active work changes the state to In Progress, duration is calculated to the second and the displayed total matches MongoDB.

cases.title: Accumulated work sessions
cases.steps: Start and stop two measured work sessions for the same ticket, then reopen the job card.
cases.expected: The total adds both sessions correctly in minutes/hours, persists after reload and has timestamped audit entries for the time records.

cases.title: Claim to resolution elapsed time
cases.steps: Record a claim time, pause active work and later resolve the ticket; compare reported durations.
cases.expected: Claim-to-resolution elapsed time is calculated and saved separately from accumulated active timer time and creation-to-closure turnaround, using approved D06 definitions.

cases.title: Resolve with mandatory summary
cases.source: FS p. 12, Resolution; TS p. 14, FR2.3
cases.steps: Attempt resolution with no summary, then enter troubleshooting steps and resolve.
cases.expected: An empty summary prevents closure; valid resolution records notes and closure time, archives the ticket from active queues and triggers the user notification.

cases.title: NWU Central IT escalation
cases.steps: Escalate a ticket with a reason and inspect the hand-off record with the supervisor.
cases.expected: Status becomes Escalated to NWU IT with reason and traceable administrative hand-off; integration records referrals without requiring write access to central IT databases.

cases.title: Chronological ticket conversation
cases.source: FS p. 12, Communication; TS p. 16, FR5.1
cases.steps: Reporter and assigned technician exchange several comments on one ticket; reload the thread.
cases.expected: Messages remain linked to the correct Ticket ID, in time order, with sender identity and timestamp; both permitted parties see the same persisted conversation.

cases.title: Comment notification to counterparty
cases.steps: Add a public technician comment, then a reporter reply; inspect both NWU inboxes.
cases.expected: Each new public comment triggers an alert to the other party with the relevant ticket link and without exposing another ticket conversation.

cases.title: Internal technician notes
cases.steps: Post an Internal Only note, then inspect the ticket and notification content as IT staff and as reporter.
cases.expected: Authorized IT staff can read the note; the student/staff reporter cannot view it in the UI, API responses or notification contents.

cases.title: Immutable communication history
cases.steps: Post comments and attempt to edit or delete the existing communication through the UI and API.
cases.expected: Posted communication remains immutable and cannot be deleted; the complete troubleshooting history persists under the approved retention approach D08.

cases.title: Ticket receipt email
cases.steps: Submit a valid ticket and inspect the generated email and delivery evidence.
cases.expected: An automatic receipt contains the unique Ticket ID and submitted summary, reaches the correct NWU inbox and links to the ticket.

cases.title: Creation claim status and resolution alerts
cases.source: FS p. 12, Notifications; TS p. 15, FR3.1-3.2
cases.steps: Create, claim, change status and resolve a ticket; capture the resulting notification for each event.
cases.expected: The NWU SMTP service dispatches correctly addressed, template-based updates for all specified events with the right status, dynamic data and direct ticket link.

cases.title: Historical search and filtering
cases.source: FS pp. 12-13, Reporting; TS p. 16, FR4.2
cases.steps: Filter historical tickets by date range, technician and hardware/category; compare selected records.
cases.expected: Only matching tickets are returned and the filters produce consistent inputs for management reports.

cases.title: Management metrics and charts
cases.steps: Use a known dataset to calculate turnaround, response times, resolution rates, category counts and workload totals.
cases.expected: Admin graphs and tables match the source data, show workload distribution and recurring faults, and use correct time definitions including creation-to-closure turnaround.

cases.title: CSV and PDF reporting
cases.steps: Apply report filters and download the report in CSV and PDF; open both downloads.
cases.expected: Both report formats contain the selected data and accurate metrics; files are readable and accessible only to the authorized role.

cases.title: Permanent ticket audit trail
cases.steps: Perform login attempts, claims, state changes, time entries and closure; review the audit data as Admin.
cases.expected: Critical actions have actor and timestamp records, every state change exists in audit_logs and each resolved ticket identifies its technician and closure time; records resist modification.

cases.title: Live status and dashboard updates
cases.steps: Open reporter and technician views in separate sessions; create a ticket, change status and post a comment.
cases.expected: Ticket lists, status and public messages update asynchronously without a full page refresh, with near real-time visibility and recorded latency.

cases.title: End to end student and staff workflow
cases.steps: As Student and Staff, submit an issue, read the receipt, reply to the technician and follow the ticket to resolution.
cases.expected: Both user groups complete the full reporting and communication workflow successfully and receive the final resolution update.

cases.title: End to end technician and Admin workflow
cases.source: FS pp. 9-13; TS pp. 14-17; PP M6
cases.steps: As Technician, claim, time, discuss and resolve a fault; as Admin, inspect its history and report.
cases.expected: All job card, notification, audit and reporting records agree for the same ticket, with role boundaries maintained throughout.

cases.title: MERN architecture and frontend baseline
cases.steps: Inspect deployed components, dependency versions and the approved frontend decision.
cases.expected: MongoDB, Express and Node.js implement persistence and backend logic. React SPA in FS versus Vanilla JavaScript in TS is resolved and evidenced under D02.

cases.title: Runtime framework and server OS
cases.steps: Record installed versions and verify startup in the target server environment.
cases.expected: Node.js is v20.x or greater; Express.js v4.x baseline is verified; target is Ubuntu Server 22.04 LTS or configured Windows Server with a Node process manager such as PM2.

cases.title: Approved hosting and local data storage
cases.source: FS pp. 7-8; TS pp. 10, 19; PP Procurement; D05
cases.steps: Inspect application/DB hosting, data locations, server allocation and available storage.
cases.expected: The approved CSIS physical/virtual host supports the runtime and persistent ticket/audit storage; data location follows the agreed university boundary and D05.

cases.title: Browser and desktop platform coverage
cases.steps: Run submission, dashboard and notification-link workflows in Chrome, Firefox, Edge and Safari on supported desktops.
cases.expected: Functional parity is recorded for Chrome/Firefox/Edge, with FS Safari coverage; Windows 10/11, macOS and Linux browser access works without client installation.

cases.title: Mobile compatibility and touch workflow
cases.steps: Use Android and iOS phones/tablets to submit, claim, time, comment and resolve tickets.
cases.expected: Mobile workflows match desktop functionality with readable responsive layouts and touch-friendly controls; FS Android 8.0+ and iOS 11.3+ support is documented or dispositioned.

cases.title: Minimum client hardware and campus network
cases.steps: Exercise workflows on a 2 GB RAM dual-core desktop at 720p and a 2 GB quad-core mobile device with a 5-inch display.
cases.expected: Core functions remain usable with keyboard/mouse or touch over stable LAN, Wi-Fi or approved mobile access; standard 10/100 campus networking is sufficient.

cases.title: NWU branding and status indicators
cases.steps: Inspect the portal, job cards and Admin views against the approved NWU identity.
cases.expected: Purple/white branding and typography are consistent; deep purple #4B2C70 primary elements, slate secondary actions and labelled green/amber/red statuses follow the specified design.

cases.title: WCAG accessibility and keyboard navigation
cases.steps: Review WCAG 2.1 evidence and manually navigate login, submission, timers, comments and reports using only the keyboard.
cases.expected: The specified WCAG 2.1 requirements, including contrast and keyboard access, are met; focus and labels support the workflows. Attach the audit scope and findings.

cases.title: Clear UI and conceptual screen coverage
cases.steps: Review the submission portal, recent tickets, job card board and analytics screen with end users.
cases.expected: Labels and errors are understandable; Log New Fault/recent-ticket access, station/priority/time details and lab/category analytics are present. Conceptual layouts are reviewed against approved designs.

cases.title: HTTP API and JSON data exchange
cases.steps: Trace browser requests for create, read and update actions using authorized technical tools.
cases.expected: REST methods such as GET, POST and PUT exchange structured JSON between browser and backend; MongoDB storage and outbound Admin metrics follow the specified data flow.

cases.title: HTTPS and TLS protection
cases.steps: Inspect web endpoints and TLS negotiation for login, ticket operations and report downloads.
cases.expected: Web traffic uses HTTPS with TLS 1.2 or higher, protecting credentials and ticket data in transit; unencrypted access cannot expose protected data.

cases.title: Secure institutional SMTP integration
cases.steps: Inspect Nodemailer configuration, relay permissions, transport encryption and test deliveries.
cases.expected: Notifications use the NWU gateway and approved NWU addresses. Port 587 with STARTTLS meets the secure baseline; any port 25 use cited in TS p. 20 has an approved encrypted relay configuration.

cases.title: Asynchronous notification processing
cases.steps: Generate multiple notification events while submitting and updating tickets; inspect delivery queue evidence.
cases.expected: Email processing does not block application requests and sustained test traffic leaves no unresolved notification backlog.

cases.title: JWT session enforcement
cases.steps: Call management APIs with a valid token, no token, an altered token and an expired token.
cases.expected: Signed JWTs establish identity and role for protected requests; invalid or absent tokens cannot claim, close or alter tickets or audit data. D01 governs reporter entry.

cases.title: Standalone authentication boundary
cases.steps: Review login dependencies and management access with central SSO unavailable.
cases.expected: Management authentication operates using the internal module; no unavailable central Active Directory/SSO API is required for the initial release. Future integrations remain separately scoped.

cases.title: Role and object authorization
cases.steps: Attempt own/other reporter reads and edits, technician ticket actions, role changes and Admin report/log access.
cases.expected: Reporters are limited to their own tickets; technicians manage approved workloads; reports/system logs and permission changes are restricted to authorized administrators. Resolve queue scope in D04.

cases.title: bcrypt credential storage
cases.steps: Inspect test-account credential records and password verification configuration with an authorized administrator.
cases.expected: Stored passwords are salted bcrypt hashes with the configured high work factor; no plaintext credential storage is present. Record configuration evidence without copying secrets.

cases.title: Server input sanitization
cases.steps: In the test environment submit malformed values, NoSQL operators and inert XSS/injection test strings through forms and API calls.
cases.expected: Server validation using express-validator prevents injection, unauthorized database access and browser script execution, including when client validation is bypassed.

cases.title: MongoDB network access restriction
cases.steps: Review database firewall/bind rules and attempt database connections from permitted and unpermitted test hosts.
cases.expected: Only the application server IP can connect to MongoDB; direct client or unapproved-host access is denied.

cases.title: Personal information purpose and protection
cases.steps: Review collected names, NWU emails, ticket content, access permissions and encryption/security evidence with the responsible reviewer.
cases.expected: Personal data supports incident resolution and follows documented POPIA and university handling controls; access and data protection evidence is attached for acceptance review.

cases.title: Retention archive and anonymization
cases.steps: Review the approved post-2026 retention procedure and exercise it on test records.
cases.expected: Records are archived or anonymized after the academic cycle according to the approved policy, while audit traceability and immutable operational history are handled as agreed in D08.

cases.title: UI response within two seconds
cases.source: FS p. 13, Performance; TS p. 22, 3.9.1; PP M4
cases.steps: Measure login, ticket acknowledgement, timer start and ordinary status/message interactions under normal network conditions.
cases.expected: Standard input responses and ticket acknowledgement are within 2.0 seconds; record timings, network conditions and any failures. PP page-load checks are also captured.

cases.title: Fifty concurrent connections
cases.steps: Run at least 50 simultaneous connections exercising submissions, status changes and notifications.
cases.expected: Service remains responsive without data corruption or service decline; capture response times, error counts and notification queue drain evidence.

cases.title: Large histories and resource efficiency
cases.steps: Load representative large ticket histories and monthly reports on older lab and mobile clients; record CPU/RAM and timings.
cases.expected: The system remains usable without client slowdown or significant lag. Record observed limits and agree a dataset and qualitative acceptance decision where no numeric budget is specified.

cases.title: Concurrent dashboard synchronization
cases.steps: Open two technician sessions, create a new fault and attempt to claim the same ticket from both sessions.
cases.expected: Polling or supported WebSockets promptly refresh both views; one consistent technician assignment is retained and conflicting claims do not overwrite each other silently.

cases.title: Functional specification availability target
cases.steps: Review monitoring logs for the agreed academic-hours observation window and calculate uptime.
cases.expected: Measure against the FS target of 99.9% during standard academic hours; record window, downtime and result separately from the technical target until D03 is approved.

cases.title: Technical availability and downtime target
cases.steps: Review logs for 07:30-18:00 Monday-Friday and semester unplanned downtime.
cases.expected: Measure both TS requirements: 98% uptime in that window and no more than 9.5 hours unplanned downtime per semester. Record period and resolve the differing targets under D03.

cases.title: Unassisted student learnability
cases.steps: Have 10 new students independently submit a fault without training or verbal assistance; record each elapsed time.
cases.expected: All 10 students submit successfully without verbal help and each submission takes less than 60 seconds; attach participant timing evidence.

cases.title: Hazard priority and visual alert
cases.steps: Submit safe test descriptions of live-wire/burning-equipment hazards and inspect the technician dashboard.
cases.expected: Physical-risk tickets receive Critical/Hazardous priority and a prominent red labelled alert for immediate attention; no actual hazardous equipment is needed for testing.

cases.title: Recurring hardware fault visibility
cases.steps: Create recurring hardware-failure examples for the same lab location/server rack and inspect historical reports.
cases.expected: Technicians and management can identify repeated location-specific failures for investigation, including potential overheating/cooling patterns.

cases.title: Crash safe ticket updates
cases.steps: In an isolated test environment interrupt a status update, recover the service and inspect ticket and audit data.
cases.expected: Transactional handling restores the last known good state or a fully committed update; no partial or lost hazard ticket remains.

cases.title: Unanswered physical hazard escalation
cases.steps: Set and record the approved hazard timeout, leave a Physical Hazard test ticket unanswered and observe escalation.
cases.expected: At the predetermined interval the Lab Manager receives the escalation notification. Thirty minutes is an example in TS, not a fixed threshold until approved.

cases.title: Safety records and reminders
cases.steps: Review a hardware fault submission and retrieve the hazard handling history with the safety reviewer.
cases.expected: The form displays approved NWU laboratory safety reminders; digital records show reported hazards and actions for the institution safety review and OHSA evidence.

cases.title: Daily automated database backups
cases.steps: Inspect backup schedules, logs and artifacts for consecutive 24-hour windows.
cases.expected: MongoDB backups run automatically and successfully at least once per 24-hour window; evidence identifies the latest recoverable backup.

cases.title: Restore within two hours
cases.steps: Restore a backup into an isolated environment using the documented procedure; time the operation and validate records.
cases.expected: The database returns to its last known good backed-up state within 2 hours, with ticket, user, time-log and audit integrity verified.

cases.title: Endpoint documentation and code quality
cases.steps: Review all backend endpoints, code comments, schema naming and static analysis results.
cases.expected: Every endpoint has JSDoc or Swagger documentation; ESLint or equivalent reports no critical style violations. snake_case data names and PascalCase modules follow TS conventions or documented exceptions.

cases.title: Developer onboarding and modular maintenance
cases.steps: Give a new maintainer the README and repository; time setup and review separation of major modules.
cases.expected: The maintainer can run the application in less than 20 minutes using the README; commented modular code supports future maintenance and deployment to other departments.

cases.title: End user help and manuals
cases.source: FS p. 9, User Documentation; TS pp. 11-12
cases.steps: Open the quick-start PDF, login-page FAQ and user/technician/Admin manuals; follow a workflow from each.
cases.expected: Help covers access/login and password recovery, submission/categories, ticket status, timer use, secure comments, reports, user roles and troubleshooting in clear visual steps.

cases.title: Technical documentation and models
cases.steps: Review the handover set and referenced analysis models against the release.
cases.expected: Architecture, ERD, state transitions, wireframes, schemas, server deployment, SMTP setup and failure troubleshooting are available, current and professionally typed; external references follow NWU Harvard style.

cases.title: Version control and update delivery
cases.steps: Review GitHub history, repository documentation and the departmental deployment/update procedure.
cases.expected: Source and technical documents are version controlled, secure SSH/HTTPS supports repository access and the documented update process delivers the approved release to the departmental server.

cases.title: Zero licence cost and launch scope
cases.source: FS p. 8; TS p. 11, 2.5.2-2.5.3; PP Financial Plan
cases.steps: Review production dependencies, service plans and permitted deployment audience.
cases.expected: The release uses approved free/open-source tooling and university resources with zero new licensing costs; initial launch is restricted to CSIS labs/offices within the 2026 scope.

cases.title: Automated API and security acceptance evidence
cases.source: PP Acceptance Plan M3; Quality Plan
cases.steps: Review the release automated API/unit test suite and security assessment.
cases.expected: Automated API tests have a 100% pass rate and there are zero critical security vulnerabilities; attach the release-specific reports.

cases.title: One hundred user performance exercise
cases.source: PP Quality Plan, Performance Load Testing; D07
cases.steps: Simulate up to 100 users performing representative workflows and capture response-time and integrity results.
cases.expected: The project-plan sub-2.0-second response target is assessed at the 100-user profile; retain this evidence separately from the TS minimum of 50 connections.

cases.title: Resolution email within two minutes
cases.source: PP Appendix A UAT-03; FS p. 12
cases.steps: Change a test ticket to Resolved; record trigger, dispatch and inbox arrival times.
cases.expected: The resolution email dispatches within 2 minutes of the trigger. Record inbox arrival separately so dispatch and delivery are distinguishable.

cases.title: Infrastructure and relay readiness
cases.source: FS p. 16 ISS-02; TS p. 28 ISS-001/002; PP Procurement
cases.steps: Review the allocated host, database access, network paths, SMTP credentials and relay permission evidence.
cases.expected: The dedicated environment and email relay are provisioned and verified; unresolved dependencies have owners and cannot be recorded as passed without evidence.

cases.title: Operational transfer and deployment verification
cases.source: PP Appendix D; Acceptance Plan M7
cases.steps: Review repository ownership, VM/SSH and MongoDB access transfer with the CSIS Network Administrator; verify deployed workflows.
cases.expected: The permanent maintainer receives ownership/access through secure channels, environment/IP/connection documentation and user guides; sponsor reviews deployment and handover evidence.

cases.title: User adoption and escalation readiness
cases.source: FS p. 16 ISS-01/03/04/06; PP Risk Plan
cases.steps: Review assigned maintenance capacity, the approved NWU escalation procedure and transition from the legacy support mailbox.
cases.expected: A support owner, clear user guide and escalation hand-off exist; the planned automatic legacy-mailbox reply directs users to the portal and outstanding project issues have recorded actions.

cases.title: Future file attachments
cases.steps: Review architecture and any separately approved attachment scope.
cases.expected: The design can be extended to screenshot/log uploads; implemented upload functionality is a future enhancement unless explicitly included in this release.

cases.title: Optional offline queue viewing
cases.steps: Review service-worker/cache design and, only if implemented, view a queue during a simulated disconnection.
cases.expected: Offline access is optional/future scope; record implementation evidence or an approved N/A disposition without making it a current mandatory gate.

cases.title: Optional browser printing
cases.steps: If in scope, use browser print on a job card or solution report.
cases.expected: The optional printed output is readable through standard OS/browser printing; otherwise record approved N/A.

cases.title: Future Outlook or central system integrations
cases.steps: Review proposed integration boundaries and MFA/SSO dependencies with the supervisor.
cases.expected: Future Outlook/calendar and full central-system integration remain separately approved work; initial escalation record and local management login remain testable without them.
